
---
title: Serialization format of analyses
---


## Block structure

Syntactic analyses produce a list of `Sentence` objects, `VerbalExpression` objects, and `TokenAnalysis` objects. These are serialized to a plain-text format with delimited-text data blocks identified by labels for each, identified by the labels `#!sentences`, `#!verbal_units` and `#!tokens` respectively. A fourth, optional block with metadata about the language model and its reasoning is identified by the label `#!lm`. Blocks may appear in any order and may repeat. (This means it that concatenating data from multiple analyses results in a valid serialization). 

The delimited-text structure of each block's data directly translates the structure of the object it is serializing. `None` fields are serialized as an empty string (`""`). By default, the pipe character `|` is used as a delimiter in delimited-text blocks.

## Field structure of each block

The structure of each block type is illustrated with the serialization of an analysis of a passage with text content `arma virumque cano` and CTS URN `urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1`.

### `#!sentences`

Sentence blocks have four columns with a header `context_begin|first_token|context_end|last_token`. These give the URN context and token ID of the first and last tokens of each sentence.


**Example**:

```
#!sentences
context_begin|first_token|context_end|last_token
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t0|urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t4
```



### `#!verbal_units`

Verbal unit blocks begin with a header `context|token|syntactic_type`. The token that the verbal expression is anchored to is identified by a CTS URN plus token ID.  


**Example**:

```
#!verbal_units
context|token|syntactic_type
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t3|independent
```


### `#!tokens`

Token analysis blocks begin with a header `context|id|tokentype|text|lemma|related|relationship`.


Entries in the table for tokens are *ordered* by the position of the token in document order. Each token is identified by a CTS URN plus token ID, followed by the surface form appearing in the passage and a lemma (headword). The graph structure is recorded by two fields identifying a token by its ID, and classifying the relationship of the two tokens. 


Tokens that are syntactically related to more than one node in the syntax graph have one row for each relation. Each repeated row will have the same values for `context`, `id`, `tokentype`, `text` and `lemma`: only the values of
`related` and `relationship` will differ. These rows must appear together to satisfy the requirement that tokens appear in document order, but the sequence of rows for a token with multiple relations is not specified.


In a successful analysis, all non-punctuation tokens have a value for `related` and `relationship`. Punctuation tokens appear in the table but are not related to any element of the syntax graph.  

**Example**: *arma virumque cano.*

The coordinating word *que* relates to both *arma* and *virum*. It therefore appears twice in the table. This is a valid serialization:

```
#!tokens
context|id|tokentype|text|lemma|related|relationship
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t0|lexical|arma|arma|t3|direct object
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t1|lexical|virum|vir|t3|direct object
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t2|enclitic|que|que|t0|coordinating word
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t2|enclitic|que|que|t1|coordinating word
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t3|lexical|cano|cano|root|unit verb
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t4|punctuation|.|||
```


The following table has identical contents except that the sequence of two lines for token `t2` is reversed.  This is also a valid serialization since the unique set of tokens appears in document order, and the sequence of rows for the multiple entries for *que* is not specified.


```
#!tokens
context|id|tokentype|text|lemma|related|relationship
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t0|lexical|arma|arma|t3|direct object
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t1|lexical|virum|vir|t3|direct object
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t2|enclitic|que|que|t1|coordinating word
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t2|enclitic|que|que|t0|coordinating word
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t3|lexical|cano|cano|root|unit verb
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t4|punctuation|.|||
```


Implied tokens have no specified order since they do not appear in the text: they may be added to the table at any point.


**Example with implied token**: *omnia praeclara rara.*

This complete sentence has an implied form of *sum* for its main verb. The following table includes an entry with token type `implied sum` in the fourth data line, and is a valid serialization of the analysis, but the token `t2_implied` could have been placed in any sequence in the table.


```
#!tokens
context|id|tokentype|text|lemma|related|relationship
|t0|lexical|omnia|omnis|t2_implied|subject
|t1|lexical|praeclara|praeclarus|t0|adjectival
|t2|lexical|rara|rarus|t2_implied|predicate
|t2_implied|implied sum||sum|root|unit verb
|t3|punctuation|.|||
```

### `#!lm`



The optional `#!lm` block is shaped differently. It has three `KEY=value` lines per sentence with keys (`MODEL`, `CONTEXT` and `REASONING`). These record the model that producse the analysis, the sentence, identified as a URN range, and the model's reasoning (collapsed to one line).

```
#!lm
MODEL=litellm_proxy/anthropic/Claude Opus 5
CONTEXT=urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1.t0-urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1.t3
REASONING="arma virumque cano" = "I sing of arms and a man." The only verbal expression is the finite verb "cano" (1st sg. present indicative active), an independent main verb, transitive active, with relatedtoken1 = 'root'. "arma" (neuter accusative plural) and "virum" (accusative singular) are both direct objects of "cano". The enclitic "-que" (here tokenized separately as "que") is a coordinating conjunction joining the two nouns: relatedtoken1 -> "arma", relatedtoken2 -> "virum", both relations 'coordinating conjunction'. Each noun independently keeps its own 'direct object' relation to "cano". No implied tokens are needed; no ambiguity of note ("virum" could theoretically be a genitive plural of "vir", but "arma virumque cano" is unambiguously accusative singular here as a second object of "cano").


```
